text:
maria: ran an nsys trace on the canary traffic after last night's rollout. seeing large queue-only spikes (~100-150ms) even though compute per-request is ~40ms. trace: https://perfetto.internal/trace/1765432100
nsys cmd: ```nsys profile -o batchtrace --trace=cuda,osrt --capture-range=cuda --sample=cpu,osrt --force-overwrite --output=run1```. uploaded artifacts to artifacts.internal/1765432100/run1.nsys

raj: quick skim — I think kernel selection is bouncing. trace shows fallback to smaller-width kernel for some seq lengths. excerpt: `KernelSelect::chosen=cutlass_int8 (fallback) launches=3 extra-launch-overhead=18us`

kevin: timeline snapshot looks like queue stretches before matmul start. snippet from perfetto: ```GPU queue: enqueue=110us -> kernel_launch=5us -> compute=40us -> post-kernel queue-stall=120us``` That's consistent with batch window being too permissive/long and causing coalescing that increases launch overhead for small kernels.

sophia: also seeing a kvcache warmup / sweep wave around the same period. kvcache miss rate jumped from ~2% to ~18% after the rollout. perf markers: `kvcache.sweep start/stop`, a lot of prefetch + evict churn. config changed `kvcache.max_segments` in rollout?

raj: good call @sophia. if the kvcache segmentation dropped, cache locality suffers and we re-prefetch which makes request variance wider -> kernel selector sees a broader seq-length distribution and ends up picking fallback kernels. also launch count goes up.

maria: can someone run a focused nsys with env overrides: `REDWOOD_BATCH_WINDOW_MS=4 REDWOOD_PREFETCH_THREADS=2 KVCACHE_DEBUG=1` on staging? use `--nsys-collect-opts='--capture-range=cuda'` so we can isolate the GPU timeline. i'll repro locally but want a staging profile.

kevin: ran quick staging jobs. results: with `batch_window=4ms` queue p95 dropped from ~230ms -> ~60ms, compute p50 increased ~5% (tiny). so there's a clear tradeoff: reducing window reduces queue tail dramatically at cost of a bit more compute (less coalescing benefits). logs: `batch_window_ms=8 -> 12ms` was worst.

deploy-bot: rollout note: 2026-03-17T21:10 UTC canary=43% traffic. config diff: `batch_window_ms: 10 -> 12` in the rollout manifest.

maria: action items:
- revert the batch_window change in canary immediately
- run targeted kvcache warmup perf test and collect nsys profiles for window=4/8/12ms
- add telemetry metric `runtime.kernel_path` so we can count kernel choices per seq-length bucket

raj: I'll open a tiny PR to revert the batch_window change and add the `runtime.kernel_path` metric. tagging @kevin to upload the nsys artifacts and perfetto links into the PR.

kevin: uploaded traces and perfetto link: https://artifacts.internal/trace/1765432100/run1.nsys , https://artifacts.internal/trace/1765432100/run2.nsys and perfetto view https://perfetto.internal/trace/1765432100/view . added short note in PR with images of the kernel timeline. :thumbsup:

sophia: note for Dedicated customers: if we revert window we should A/B with throughput SLA gating. for some workload mixes the larger window was improving throughput. propose a conservative rollback + opt-in AB test for Dedicated.

maria: agreed. i'll coordinate with oncall to apply the rollback for canary and schedule perf runs tomorrow 09:00 PST. leaving this thread open for updates, will close after rollback confirmation.
